Brief Hospital Course:
This is a ___ year old male with a history of atrial 
fibrillation, chronic constipation, and hypertension who 
presents with hypotension and a distended abdomen. 

1) Abdominal Distension: Upon admission patient's abdomen 
demonstrated distension on examination. Abdominal CT scans on 
___ and ___ showed large bowel dilation with gas and fluid. 
There were no masses noted on these studies, however, rectal 
masses could not be ruled out. Initially we felt that this 
distension was secondary to exacerbation of chronic constipation 
versus pseudo-obstruction versus obstructing mass effect. On 
___ abdominal distension and abdominal pain worsened. In 
addition, patient spiked fever to 101 and was noted to have WBC 
count of 20. His clinical worsening was substantiated by 
interval worsening of bowel dilation on his Abd CT from that 
day. Patient was noted to have liquid stool, suspicious for 
CDiff, as well. Patient was started on empiric treatment for 
Clostridium dificile colitis with IV Flagyl and PO Vancomycin. 
He was concurrently started on broad coverage for possible 
pneumonia, as well, given patient's risk of aspiration and our 
uncertainty of what was contributing to his fever and elevated 
white blood cell count. Within 24 hours of initiating CDiff 
therapy along with broad spectrum pneumonia coverage the 
patient's abdominal distension had improved, he was no longer 
febrile, and his white count was trending down. To date CDiff 
titers have been negative x 1. Empiric treatment is being 
continued given our strong suspicion and the patient's 
relatively rapid recovery after beginning treatment. Patient was 
seen by gastroenterology who agree with this decision. They 
recommend continuing the patient on a 14 day course of PO 
Vancomycin. They also recommend that the patient undergo 
colonoscopy approximately 6 weeks from discharge to assess for 
any masses that could have possibly contributed to this event. 
At time of discharge, abdominal distension had completely 
resolved. The patient's abdomen was soft, he had bowel sounds, 
and had a bowel movement prior to discharge. Patient was also 
tolerating a pureed, nectar thickened liquid diet.  A second 
stool was sent for Cdiff which is pending and will need to be 
followed up.

2) Hypotension: Patient was noted to be mildly hypotensive in 
the emergency department with a pressure of 90/63. He was 
bolused with IVF and had a nasal gastric tube that was placed to 
suction and his pressures increased to systolic over 100. On the 
floor the patient remained normotensive. Unclear if hypotension 
at the patient's nursing home related to abdominal distension 
leading to decreased pressures by reducing cardiac filling 
pressure. Blood pressure remained stable during rest of 
admission and did not require further fluid boluses.

3)Bibasilar consolidation on CT Abdomen: As noted above, patient 
found to have evidence of bibasilar consolidation on CT abdomen 
from ___ given this finding occurred in the setting of the 
patient spiking a fever and having an elevated white blood cell 
count he was started on empiric treatment for a hospital 
acquired pneumonia with IV Vancomycin and IV Zosyn. The 
patient's oxygen saturation remained in the high 90's throughout 
the patient's hospitalization. He did not develop a cough and 
otherwise remained hemodynamically stable. As mentioned above, 
the patient's fever resolved within 24 hours and white cell 
blood count trended down to normal. The Vancomycin was stopped 
within 48 hours and the Zosyn was changed to Ciprofloxacin. 
Suspicion for pneumonia remains uncertain. At baseline the 
patient is a chronic aspirator and is imobile which could 
account for consolidative lung changes and poor perfusion at the 
lung bases. The patient was continued his remaining two days of 
Ciprofloxacin to complete a seven day course of antibiotics. 

4)Chronic Constipation: Patient's abdominal distension certainly 
could have been a manifestation of chronic constipation 
exacerbation. While patient's large bowel was distended bowel 
regimen was held. When colonic distension began to resolve 
patient was slowly restarted on bowel regimen. Gastroenterology 
recommended the addition of Miralax 17 g daily. The patient did 
produce 3+ bowel movements during this admission, the last one 
being on the day of discharge. Patient should continue his 
current bowel regimen with the addition of daily Miralax. 

5)History of Stroke and Deep Venous Thrombosis: Patient was 
continued on his outpatient regimen of Coumadin. There was 
concern that the patient's right leg appeared swollen compared 
to the left though a lower extremity ultrasound ruled out deep 
venous thrombosis. INR must continued to be monitored regularly 
for proper coumadin dosing.

6)Diabetes: Blood sugars remained stable during this admission. 
The patient was continued on his outpatient sliding scale.

7)Hypertension: Stable during this admission. The patient was 
continued on his outpatient dose of Lisinopril and furosemide.

8)Neuropathic Pain: Stable during this admission. Patient was 
continued on his home dose of gabapentin and morphine sulfate 
immediate release. He was started on lidoderm patches to his 
right foot which he felt was beneficial for pain relief. Would 
suggest continuing lidoderm patches daily to optimize pain 
relief.

9)Hypothyroidism: Stable during this admission. He was continued 
on his home dose of levothyroxine. Would suggest rechecking a 
TSH/free T4 as an outpatient- felt being an inpatient would 
confound results so not checked.

10)Hyperlipidemia: Stable during this admission. Patient was 
continued on his home dose of simvastatin.

11) Depression: Stable during this admission. Patient was 
continued on his home dose of mirtazipine.

12)Iron Deficiency Anemia: Anemia stable during this admission. 
Ferrous sulfate was held given patient's possible infections. 
Would suggest holding ferrous sulfate for at least two weeks. 

13) Swallowing: During this admission patient was screened by 
speech and swallow and underwent a videoesophageal swallow test. 
It was recommended that he continue with teaspoons of nectar 
thickened liquids and small bites of puree consistencies. he 
will continue to require 1:1 supervision with meals. In addition 
it is recommended that he receive he pills crushed with purees.

14)Back pressure ulcers: The following recommendations were made 
by our wound care consult team: Patient should have a atmos air 
mattress, turn and reposition every ___ hours and prn off 
coccyx. Heels off bed surface at all times. Multipodis Splints  
to B/L ___. If OOB, limit sit time to one hour at a time and 
sit on a pressure relief cushion 4"" Foam. He should elevate ___ 
while sitting and moisturize bilateral lower extremities and 
feet BID with Aloe Vesta Moisture Barrier Ointment.

Patient was FULL code during this admission.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the hospital because your blood pressure 
was low and your abdomen was noted to be distended. Imaging of 
your abdomen did not reveal that you had an obstruction in your 
bowel. We felt that you may have had an infection in your bowel 
that was causing it to be very dilated, however, we do not yet 
have laboratory evidence of this. We did however, determine that 
you had a fever and your white blood cell count or immune 
response was suggestive of an infection. We treated you 
empirically for a gut infection with antibiotics. We also 
treated you empirically for a pneumonia because your CT scan 
implied that you may have an area of infection in your lungs. 
After we initiated this antibiotic treatment your abdominal 
distension resolved. There are still lab tests pending at your 
time of discharge. We are continuing you on a 14 day course of 
the antibiotics for your gut and we are continuing you on two 
more day of therapy for a possible pneumonia or lung infection. 

We also felt that your abdominal distension could have been due 
to your chroninc constipation. We are pleased that you were able 
to have multiple bowel movements during your admission. We 
suggest you continue your current bowel regimen. We have added 
one new medication listed below.

We also addressed your chronic neuropathic pain. You expressed 
that in addition to your home pain regimen, a treatment called a 
lidocaine patch improved your pain on your right foot.

IMPRESSION:  Limited study demonstrating marked bowel dilatation.  Further

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH CONTRAST

HISTORY:  ___ man with abdominal distention and bloody nasogastric
tube output.  Please evaluate for fluid and bowel obstruction.

COMPARISON:  Portable abdomen from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Contiguous axial imaging was performed from the lung bases through
the pubic symphysis following administration of intravenous and oral contrast.
Coronal and sagittal reformatted images were also prepared.

CT OF THE ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST:  There are bilateral dependent areas of
consolidation which could represent atelectasis but is also suspicious for
bilateral aspiration pneumonia.  There are no pleural effusions.  There are no
pericardial effusions.

The spleen, adrenals, and pancreas are unremarkable.  There is mild biliary
dilatation.  There is a hypodensity within the left lobe of the liver (2:14)
which is too small to characterize by CT.  The patient is status post
cholecystectomy, and there are surgical clips within the gallbladder fossa.
There are multiple scattered hypodensities within the right and left kidneys
which are too small to characterize by CT.  The kidneys appear slightly
atrophic.  However, they do enhance and excrete contrast symmetrically, and
there is no hydronephrosis.  There is no free air.  There is no free fluid.
There is no significant retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy.  The
stomach is normal in appearance.  There is a nasogastric tube present within
the stomach, and there is a percutaneous gastrostomy tube present within the
stomach that extends through the left anterior abdominal wall.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:  The rectum is fluid filled, and there is an
air-fluid level present within a dilated and redundant sigmoid colon.  Dilated
loops of sigmoid colon measure 9.7 cm in greatest dimension.  The bladder is
distended with urine and is unremarkable in appearance.  There is contrast
that opacifies nondilated loops of small bowel.  There is contrast seen within
the cecum.  However, there is no contrast visualized within the more distal
loops of dilated large bowel.  There is no clear transition point identified.
There are calculi within the prostate.  There is no free air.  There is no
free fluid.  There is no significant pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

BONE WINDOWS:  There is a right acetabular and right femoral hip prosthesis.
There are bilateral bridging osteophytes at the sacroiliac joints.  There are
no fractures identified.  There are no suspicious sclerotic or lytic lesions
identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Dilated loops of distal large bowel with fluid present within a dilated
rectum and sigmoid colon.  There is no dilation of proximal loops of small
bowel which are filled with contrast.  Would recommend further followup with
plain films to evaluate for movement of contrast into the sigmoid colon and
rectum to rule out for possible obstruction.  These findings could also
represent an obstructing mass within the rectum which is not visualized on CT
and would recommend clinical correlation.
2.  Bilateral lung dependent consolidations could represent atelectasis or
focal areas of aspiration.
3.  Patient is status post cholecystectomy.  There is mild biliary dilatation.
4.  There is a hypodensity within the left lobe of the liver that is too small
to characterize by CT and would recommend ultrasound for further evaluation.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, the patient has taken a much

HISTORY:  Chronic constipation with abdominal distention.  Evaluate for bowel

UPRIGHT AND SUPINE ABDOMINAL RADIOGRAPHS:

FINDINGS:  Since prior examination, there has been progression of oral
contrast into the dilated loops of large bowel which are slightly increased in
size on today's examination, measuring up to 9 cm within the redundant sigmoid
colon (previously 7 cm).  Surgical clips and G-tube are unchanged.  No
evidence of pneumatosis or pneumoperitoneum.  Bibasilar atelectasis is again

IMPRESSION:

Slight interval worsening in degree of large-bowel distention with interval
progression of oral contrast within, now within the ascending colon.  Findings
may reflect patient's underlying constipation/dysmotility with a distal large-
bowel obstruction felt less likely given the CT appearance.

HISTORY:  ___ man with AFib, diabetes mellitus, chronic constipation
with worsening abdominal distention, increasing abdominal pain, seen by GI who
think this could be diverticulitis versus mass that has caused perforation.

TECHNIQUE:  5-mm contiguous axial images from the lung bases through the
lesser trochanters with IV contrast and Gastrografin contrast instilled via
the G-tube were obtained.  Coronal and sagittal reconstructions were included
in this study.  Comparison is made to a prior CT scan of the abdomen and
pelvis dated ___.

FINDINGS:  There has been interval worsening of the bibasilar consolidations
since the prior exam.  No evidence of pericardial or pleural effusion.
Atherosclerotic disease is seen in the coronary arteries, aortic valve and
aorta.

CT ABDOMEN WITH CONTRAST: Stable hypoattenuating lesions are again seen in the
liver. These lesions likely represent hepatic cysts.  Note is made of mild
stable intrahepatic bile duct dilation.  The patient is status post
cholecystectomy.

Pancreas, spleen and adrenal glands appear normal.  Hypoattenuating lesions
are noted in the kidneys bilaterally and likely represent renal cysts. No
evidence of hydronephrosis.

No evidence of free fluid or free air in the abdomen or pelvis.

Small bowel is unremarkable.  The colon is dilated with fluid and air. This
dilation is most prominent in the sigmoid colon which measures up to
approximately 9.6 cm.  No evidence of colonic diverticulosis.  No evidence of
colonic volvulus or focal transition zone.  The dilation of the large bowel
extends to the level of the rectum and no obvious mass is visualized.

CT PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST:  Bladder is decompressed around a Foley catheter.
Prostate gland is unremarkable.  No evidence of pelvic or inguinal
lymphadenopathy. There are small bilateral fat-containing inguinal hernias.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:  The patient is status post right hip arthroplasty.
Multilevel degenerative changes are seen in the lower thoracic and lumbar
spine.  No suspicious osteolytic or osteoblastic lesions are appreciated.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Interval worsening of the bibasilar consolidations since the prior exam.
2.  No evidence of bowel perforation or colonic diverticulosis.
3.  There is dilation of the colon which is most prominent in the sigmoid
colon measuring up to 9.6 cm.  No evidence of volvulus or clear transition
point.  No obvious masses are visualized.

As compared to the recent study of one day earlier, there is persistent
massive distention of air-filled loops of bowel, continuing to measure about 9
cm in greatest dimension.  There is apparent visualization of both sides of
the bowel wall, concerning for possible free intraperitoneal air, but this
could potentially be mimicked by the presence of oral contrast within the
bowel. Additionally, there is a suggestion of visualization of the crura which
could represent retroperitoneal gas or fat outlining these structures.
Considering the clinical concern for free intraperitoneal air, confirmatory
upright or lateral decubitus view of the abdomen would be helpful.
Alternatively, CT could be performed if the patient is unable to cooperate
with these maneuvers. Findings communicated by telephone with Dr. ___
on ___ by telephone.

HISTORY:  ___ male with constipation and abdominal distention found to
have colonic dilation on CT exam.  Please evaluate for free air suspected on
today's radiograph.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis one day prior and abdominal radiograph
earlier the same day.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial imaging was performed from the diaphragm to the pubic
symphysis without IV contrast.  Coronal and sagittal reformations were
provided.

CT ABDOMEN WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  Bibasilar consolidations are unchanged.  Mild
biliary dilatation and cystic hepatic lesions are also unchanged.  The spleen,
pancreas, adrenal glands, and small bowel are unremarkable.  Contrast has
passed yet further throughout the colon, and there has been improvement in the
degree of colonic dilation.  In maximal transverse dimension, the sigmoid
colon now measures 5.3 cm, which is not considered dilated (9.6 cm yesterday).
There is no evidence of colonic perforation or abdominal free air.  There has
been previous cholecystectomy.  There is no evidence of hydronephrosis.
Hypoattenuating lesions in the kidneys are unchanged.

CT PELVIS WITHOUT IV CONTRAST:  A Foley catheter remains in the bladder, with
expected air from instrumentation.  The prostate gland demonstrates a few
calcifications.  There is no pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy.  Small
bilateral fat-containing inguinal hernias are unchanged.

The abdominal aorta and its branches demonstrate numerous calcifications.

A right hip arthroplasty and multilevel degenerative changes in the thoracic
and lumbar spine are unchanged.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of colonic perforation.

2.  Resolution of colonic dilation, with continued passage of oral contrast
now in the rectum.

3.  No other change since one day prior.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of patient with massively distended
abdomen, suspected free air.

The study demonstrates multiple borderline slightly dilated loops of large
bowel up to 10 cm at the level of the cecum and approximately 7 cm at the
level of the sigmoid.  Extensive amount of oral contrast is demonstrated.  No
free air is seen.  The patient's gastrostomy is again noted.

The patient is after total replacement of the right hip.

in bowel dilation.

is seen throughout the length of the colon, with air also seen within small
bowel loops.  The overall extent of the caliber of the large bowel is improved
from ___.  There is no free intraperitoneal air or pneumatosis.

large bowel.

INDICATION:  ___ male with CVA, AFib, and questionable aspiration.
Study is a swallowing video fluoroscopic evaluation performed in conjunction
with the speech pathology department under continuous video fluoroscopy,
barium of various consistencies were administered orally to the patient.

ORAL PHASE:  Bolus formation, bolus control are moderately reduced.  Oral
transit time was mildly to moderately increased.  Premature spillage was seen
in the pharynx.

PHARYNGEAL PHASE:  There was a delay in the initiation of the swallow trigger.
Moderate laryngeal elevation and epiglottic deflection were seen.  The
laryngeal valve closure was also mildly reduced.  Mild residue remained within
the valleculae and peritoneum sinus.

ASPIRATION/PENETRATION.  Penetration was noted with nectar thick liquids and
honey-thick liquid, which cleared spontaneously.  Episode of gross aspiration
noted to occur during swallow on sips of nectar thick liquid, thin liquids,
and ground solids.  Only one episode of reflexive cough was noted with gross
aspiration whereas the rest of the episodes were silent and patient was unable
to elicit voluntary cough.

IMPRESSION:  Penetration and aspiration with various consistencies of barium
as described above.  Please see the speech pathology note on CareWeb for
detailed report and further recommendations.
